influences.name: Sting
influences.context: Seeing the tour from the inside and watching Sting perform live every night has been surreal... Being part of the Sting tour is a once-in-a-lifetime experience — he's so inspiring and generous.

influences.name: Trevor Horn
influences.context: Trevor Horn is an incredible producer and writer... During soundcheck, he told me he appreciated my attention to detail in the production — that meant the world to me.

influences.name: Kevin Parker
influences.context: I love that Kevin Parker is like a one-man band. He produces and plays everything himself — that's something I really aspire to do.

influences.name: Hitchcock
influences.context: I always talk about Hitchcock, because to me, he's someone whose subject matter is really dark and hideous, but it always looks amazing.

influences.name: Orson Welles
influences.context: I read somewhere else that some other filmmaker said the same thing about waiting for magic. It might have been Orson Welles.

influences.name: Charli XCX
influences.context: When you first start working with someone you're learning a lot about them quite quickly and that can be exciting.

influences.name: Diplo
influences.context: But that situation, working with Diplo, showed me that my process was quite different.

influences.name: A.G. Cook
influences.context: That's one thing that [PC Music producer] A.G. Cook was playing around with on the Charli XCX mixtape Pop 2: trying to make each individual section feel like the artist themselves.

influences.name: Aphex Twin
influences.context: It's like what Aphex Twin said about Windowlicker, or all of the Chris Cunningham [video] collaborations

influences.name: Chris Cunningham
influences.context: It's like what Aphex Twin said about Windowlicker, or all of the Chris Cunningham [video] collaborations

influences.name: Pharrell
influences.context: I was watching a conversation with Pharrell and Timbaland – I think it might have been on Beats 1 – and they're talking about the time in Virginia when they were making this music.

influences.name: Timbaland
influences.context: I was watching a conversation with Pharrell and Timbaland – I think it might have been on Beats 1 – and they're talking about the time in Virginia when they were making this music.

influences.name: Throbbing Gristle
influences.context: In a way it takes something from industrial music and Throbbing Gristle – there's definitely a through-line to [the idea of] sound as a valid material in pop music.

influences.name: Leroy Burgess
influences.context: I would be really curious to know how Leroy Burgess was working. He's a boogie producer, from the late '70s and early '80s. I always talk about the same people, but that's who I like!

influences.name: Stevie Wonder
influences.context: I think he was quite influenced by Stevie Wonder. His understanding of the piano… There's a virtuosity to it that is then applied to newer technology, in terms of new analogue keyboards.

influences.name: Bloodpop
influences.context: Bloodpop did the production and I said the same to him the other day: that it's such a good vibe to bring into the universe at this present moment. I've always talked to him about 'summer house' tracks
